content: Abstract:The exploration of primitive bodies in the solar system\, such as asteroids and comets\, is driven by scientific questions about the early solar system\, long-term goals of utilizing primitive body resources in space\, and the protection of the planet from hazardous impacts. content: Abstract:Thermal conductivity is a basic and familiar property of materials: silver spoons conduct heat well and plastic does not. High thermal conductivity is desirable for heat exchangers and thermal management while low thermal conductivity is needed for thermal insulation. In recent years\, the combined efforts of materials scientists\, engineers\, physicists\, and chemists have succeeded in pushing-back long-established limits in the thermal conductivity of materials. content: Abstract:Nuclear electric propulsion (NEP) offers the potential to fundamentally expand the capability and reach of spacecraft\, but realizing that potential requires overcoming significant challenges in reactor technology\, power conversion and distribution\, thermal management\, electric propulsion\, and system integration. This seminar will examine the current state of NEP development\, highlighting recent progress while exploring the demanding requirements associated with operating high-power systems continuously for years or even decades in the space environment.
title: Nuclear Electric Propulsion: Progress, Challenges, and the Path to High-Power Space Systems

content: Abstract:&nbsp\;In robotics\, we have spent a lot of time building really good maps from noisy sensor data. Who doesn’t like a nice\, crisp\, globally consistent map? Over the last 20 years\, I have been exploring a paradigm to robot navigation that eschews such globally consistent maps in favour of graphs of local maps\, which are cheaper to construct\, store\, and query. These topometric maps enable so-called teach-and-repeat (T&amp\;R) navigation. In this talk\, I will give a progress update on some of the new things we are doing with T&amp\;R including using different primary sensors\,
title: Local Maps Are All You Need!
